In 1933, Alfred Korzybski published his second book, Science and Sanity: An Introduction to Non-Aristotelian Systems and General Semantics , twelve years after his first, Manhood of Humanity . 1
Science and Sanity created a major stir among scholars and intellectuals, and in 1934, Korzybski began traveling around America to promote his work, which he referred to as general semantics (GS).
